which-app.q: Which app do I need for my climbing board?
which-app.a: Each brand has its own app: Kilter, Tension, MoonBoard, Decoy, Touchstone, Grasshopper, So iLL and Woods. Boardsesh lights all eight from one app and covers your spray wall too.

one-logbook.q: Can one app log Kilter, Tension and MoonBoard together?
one-logbook.a: Yes. Boardsesh keeps every board in one logbook, imports a Kilter or Tension account, an Aurora file or a MoonBoard CSV, and exports it all any time.

offline.a: Yes, in the iPhone, iPad and Android apps: download a board, then search, climb and log offline, and ticks sync when you're back. The browser app needs a connection.

android.q: Does it work on Android phones without Google?
android.a: Boardsesh runs on Android 7.0 or newer and doesn't check for Google certification. MoonBoard's Android app needs a Google-certified phone, and Moon support told a GrapheneOS user in January 2026 there is no plan to change that.

tablet.q: Does it work on an iPad or tablet?
tablet.a: Yes, iPad gets a sidebar, a mini player and a landscape player, and Android tablets get a sidebar rail. Kilter's and MoonBoard's iPad apps show the phone layout scaled up, and Tension's iPhone app runs scaled up on iPad.

free.a: Yes. Every feature is free for everyone, with no ads, Boardsesh doesn't sell your data, and the code is open source under Apache-2.0.

method.heading: How we compared
method.body: We make Boardsesh and say so on every page. Facts about other apps come from their own store listings, release notes and support pages, read on 2026-11-24, with a source link beside each claim. We did not test every official app on its own board, and a feature marked not documented may exist. If we got something wrong, tell us and we will fix it.

hero.lead: Boardsesh lights your Kilter Board, imports your old Aurora logbook the moment you load the file, and runs one queue for your whole crew on a phone, an iPad or a laptop. Kilter's own app is where Kilter picks its Verified climbs and curates its playlists.
hero.byline: A guide from Boardsesh. We make Boardsesh; Kilter doesn't endorse it.

verdict.heading: Which app fits your session?

pickIf.p1: You want your pre-March Kilter logbook back without a claim queue.
pickIf.p2: Your crew wants one shared queue from four different phones.
pickIf.p3: You train with pyramids, ladders and 4x4s on a rest timer.
pickIf.p4: You also climb a Tension, a MoonBoard or your own spray wall.
pickIf.p5: You run sessions from a laptop in Chrome or from an iPad.

keepIf.k1: You want Verified climbs and curated playlists picked by Kilter.
keepIf.k2: You set climbs and want Kilter's own setter credit and claims.
keepIf.k3: You want Kilter's Live at your Board view.

verdict.bottomLine: Keep both if you like: they light the same board, one phone at a time. Use Kilter's app for its curated climbs, and Boardsesh for your logbook, crew and training, free and with no ads.

free.q: Is the Kilter Board app free?
free.a: Yes. Kilter's app is free with no in-app purchases or ads listed, and Boardsesh is free for every feature, with no ads and open source code.

both.q: Can I use Boardsesh and the Kilter app on the same board?
both.a: Yes, both light the same board over Bluetooth. A Kilter board talks to one phone at a time, so disconnect one app before you connect the other.

old-logbook.q: How do I get my old Kilter logbook into a new app?
old-logbook.a: Email support@auroraclimbing.com for your JSON export, then load it in Boardsesh, where the import starts right away. Kilter's claim page takes the same file and quotes 5 to 7 business days.

not-working.q: Why is the Kilter app not working for me?
not-working.a: Kilter's support page says to update the app and restart it, and to register a new account, because old logins don't carry over. If it still fails, report it at kilterboard.io/feedback and light the board with Boardsesh in the meantime.

homewall.q: Does Boardsesh work with the Kilter Homewall?
homewall.a: Yes. Boardsesh covers Kilter Board Original and Homewall on iPhone, iPad, Android and in a Chrome or Edge browser.

tablet.q: Does it work on an iPad or tablet?
tablet.a: Yes, on iPad you get a sidebar, a mini player and a landscape player, and Android tablets get a sidebar rail. Kilter's iPad app shows its phone layout scaled up in its App Store screenshots.

hero.pill: Works with Tension, Decoy, Grasshopper, Touchstone and So iLL boards
hero.h1: Boardsesh vs the Aurora board apps
hero.lead: Tension, Decoy, Grasshopper, Touchstone and So iLL each have their own app from Aurora Climbing, with near-identical store listings. Boardsesh lights all five, keeps every brand's sends in one logbook with Kilter, MoonBoard, Woods and your spray wall, and adds a crew queue, seven workout types and a browser version. It's free, open source and has no ads.
hero.byline: A guide from Boardsesh. We make Boardsesh; board makers don't endorse it.

verdict.heading: Pick the app for your Aurora board

pickIf.p1: You climb two Aurora brands, or Kilter as well, and want one logbook
pickIf.p2: Your crew wants one queue, each climber adding picks from their own phone
pickIf.p3: You want pyramids, ladders, 4x4s or limit sessions on any Aurora brand
pickIf.p4: You climb in a garage with no signal and still want to search and log
pickIf.p5: You want an iPad layout or a laptop browser beside the wall

keepIf.k1: You use Tension's Workout AI to plan sessions from your logbook
keepIf.k2: You chase leaderboards, badges, Decoy Selects or the side-climb filter
keepIf.k3: You set problems for climbers who use your brand's own app

verdict.bottomLine: Every Aurora app is free and lights its own brand well. Boardsesh is the pick when a crew shares the wall, when you train to a plan, or when you climb more than one board.

only.heading: What Boardsesh adds to an Aurora board
only.lead: Aurora's apps each cover one brand. Boardsesh is built for the crew at the wall and the training week around it.

one-app.title: Five brands, one app
one-app.body: Aurora publishes a separate app and logbook for each brand. Boardsesh runs all five, plus Kilter, MoonBoard, Woods and spray walls; sign in to each Aurora account once and your history lands in one logbook.

crew-queue.title: A queue the whole crew fills
crew-queue.body: Up to 500 climbs, added from everyone's phone, with undo and a shared rest timer. The crew can see whose phone holds the wall's Bluetooth link.

workouts.title: Seven ways to train
workouts.body: Volume, pyramid, ladder, grade focus, On the Minute, 4x4 and limit bouldering, with warm-up and cool-down stages. In our October 2026 count, every tested plan shape filled at every core grade on Tension, Decoy and Grasshopper.

brands.heading: Five Aurora brands in Boardsesh
brands.lead: Each brand keeps its own layouts, sizes and app. Here is what Boardsesh covers for each one and what the brand's own app offers. Counts are from our October 2026 catalogue study; ratings were read on 24 November 2026.

tension.name: Tension Board
tension.summary: TB1 and both TB2 layouts. Sign in with your Tension account and your sends come into Boardsesh, with new ones following.
tension.layouts: Original Layout (TB1), Tension Board 2 Mirror, Tension Board 2 Spray
tension.sizes: 10 in all. TB1: Full Wall, Half Kickboard, No Kickboard, Short, Short & Narrow. TB2 (high x wide): 12x12, 10x12, 12x8, 10x8, 12x16. Sets A, B, C and Foot on TB1; Wood and Plastic on TB2, plus expansion sets on the 12x16
tension.angles: 0 to 70 degrees in 5 degree steps; mirror lighting on TB1 and TB2 Mirror
tension.benchmarks: At 40°: 517 on TB1, 286 on TB2 Mirror, 184 on TB2 Spray
tension.officialApp: Tension Board 2 on iOS, Tension Board on Google Play: 3.51 from 65 ratings (US App Store) and 3.30 from 80 (Google Play). Workout AI since August 2025, leaderboards since February 2026. Listed LED colours: green start, blue middle, red finish, magenta feet.

decoy.name: Decoy Board
decoy.summary: The Dungeon Trainer in three sizes. Decoy's app renamed benchmarks to Selects and has a side-climb filter that Boardsesh doesn't match.
decoy.sizes: 8x10, 8x12 and 12x12; 19 hold sets on the 12x12, from Foundation and Pacos to Limestone, and 12 on the smaller walls
decoy.angles: 0 to 70 degrees in 5 degree steps; mirror lighting supported
decoy.benchmarks: 166 at 40°; the Decoy app calls its list Selects
decoy.officialApp: Decoy Board: 5.0 from 6 ratings (US App Store) and 4.8 from 5 (Google Play). Leaderboards and badges since July 2023, Only Side Climbs since September 2023.

grasshopper.name: Grasshopper Board
grasshopper.summary: Adjustable walls that tilt past vertical into slab. Boardsesh offers the -5° setting and splits each climb's history by angle.
grasshopper.sizes: Ninja (8x10), Master (8x12) and GrandMaster (12x12), each with or without Tweeners; sets Engage, Flow, Power, Gradient, Dimension and Tweeners
grasshopper.benchmarks: 9 at 30°; the official app is the better place for Grasshopper benchmarks
grasshopper.officialApp: Grasshopper Board: 4.05 from 21 ratings (US App Store) and 4.13 from 25 (Google Play), 10K+ installs. Benchmarks, leaderboards and badges since July 2023, Only Side Climbs since September 2023.

touchstone.name: Touchstone Board
touchstone.summary: One layout in one size, so there's little to set up. Boardsesh listed 1,087 Touchstone climbs at 35°, the busiest angle.
touchstone.sizes: Full Size, with one hold set (All Holds)
touchstone.officialApp: Touchstone Board: 3.33 from 3 ratings (US App Store), none shown on Google Play, 1K+ installs. iOS version 3.9.14, released 10 February 2026.

so-ill.name: So iLL Board
so-ill.summary: Two widths of the Summer 2024 layout. Boardsesh lets you pick your own LED colour for start, hand, finish and foot holds.
so-ill.sizes: 8x12 (11 hold columns) and 12x12 (17 hold columns), both 20 rows, one hold set
so-ill.benchmarks: None in Boardsesh's catalogue; 540 climbs listed at 30°
so-ill.officialApp: So iLL Board: no ratings on the US App Store or Google Play, 1K+ installs. iOS version 3.9.14, released 10 February 2026. Listed LED colours: green start, magenta middle, cyan finish, white feet.

faq.heading: What climbers ask about the Aurora apps

free.q: Is the Tension Board app free?
free.a: Yes. Tension's app is free with no ads or purchases, like the other Aurora apps, and Boardsesh is free with every feature open to everyone.

one-app.q: Can one app run my Tension and Kilter boards?
one-app.a: Not with the official apps: Aurora ships one app per brand, and Kilter's new app covers Kilter alone. Boardsesh runs both and keeps the ticks in one logbook.

decoy.q: Does Boardsesh work with the Decoy Dungeon Trainer?
decoy.a: Yes, on the 8x10, 8x12 and 12x12, with Decoy's hold sets and angles from 0 to 70 degrees. It lights older and newer Aurora controllers.

so-ill.q: Is there a So iLL board app?
so-ill.a: Yes. Aurora Climbing publishes the free So iLL Board app for iPhone and Android, and Boardsesh also works with So iLL's Summer 2024 boards.

grasshopper.q: Does Boardsesh support the Grasshopper -5 degree setting?
grasshopper.a: Yes. Grasshopper angles in Boardsesh run from -5 to 70 degrees, and each climb's history is split by the angle you climbed it at.

import.q: Can I bring my Aurora logbook into Boardsesh?
import.a: Yes. Sign in with your account on any of the five brands' cards under Connected apps and the logbook copies one way into Boardsesh; an Aurora JSON file is the fallback for an account you can't sign in to.

method.heading: How we compared
method.body: We read the App Store and Google Play listings and version histories of all five Aurora apps, plus Tension's FAQ, on 24 November 2026. Boardsesh rows were checked against its own code and docs, and catalogue counts come from our October 2026 workout study. We didn't test any app on a physical board for this page. Boardsesh is not affiliated with Aurora Climbing or any of the five brands; if a row is wrong, tell us and we'll fix it.

meta.title: MoonBoard App Alternative: Boardsesh vs the MoonBoard App
meta.description: MoonBoard app stuck on Please Wait? Compare Boardsesh with Moon's app: 7 layouts, Benchmarks, which LEDs work, CSV import and Android without Google.

hero.pill: Works with 7 MoonBoard layouts, from 2010 to Mini 2025
hero.lead: Boardsesh lights your MoonBoard, runs the session from a phone or a browser, and logs a send without asking your height or weight. Moon's own app keeps official Benchmarks and rankings, and is rated 1.45 from 254 US App Store ratings as of 2026-11-24.
hero.byline: A guide from Boardsesh. We make Boardsesh; Moon Climbing doesn't endorse it.

verdict.heading: Which app fits your MoonBoard night?

pickIf.p1: You get 'Please Wait' on Moon's app and want to climb tonight.
pickIf.p2: You'd rather not give height, weight and age to log a send.
pickIf.p3: Your Android phone lacks Google certification; Boardsesh doesn't check.
pickIf.p4: You climb MoonBoard and other boards and want one logbook.
pickIf.p5: Your crew shares one queue, or you light the board from a browser.

keepIf.k1: You publish problems or follow official MoonBoard rankings.
keepIf.k2: You run a custom wall with Moon's hold recognition and LED mapping.

verdict.bottomLine: Keep Moon's app for publishing and rankings. Add Boardsesh for the nights Moon's app won't load, and for crew sessions, workouts and a logbook that reaches past MoonBoard.

only.heading: Where Boardsesh goes further
only.lead: Three things you get from Boardsesh on a MoonBoard. Each has a source below.

android.title: Android without Google certification
android.body: MoonBoard's Android app needs a Google-certified phone, and Moon's support told a GrapheneOS user in January 2026 there is 'no plan for the app to be changed'. Boardsesh doesn't check, and email sign-in works.

browser.title: Light the board from a browser
browser.body: Moon's website lets you log in to your account. Boardsesh's browser app at app.boardsesh.com lights the board from Chrome or Edge and runs the whole session.

one-logbook.title: One logbook for every board
one-logbook.body: Bring a Moon CSV in once and your sends sit next to your Kilter, Tension and Woods sessions, with stats across all of them.

comparison.heading: Boardsesh and the MoonBoard app, side by side
comparison.lead: Checked 2026-11-24. Moon's app wins the rows that need its controllers or its moderators.

lighting.boardsesh: Lights the wall from the app or Chrome; on screen, holds glow in their LED colours
lighting.official: Lights the wall from the app; on screen, rings with START and END labels

benchmarks.boardsesh: Moon's Benchmarks, imported in batches: 295 to 570 per layout, with a filter.
benchmarks.official: Curated by a small group of Moon moderators; new ones appear here first.

publishing.boardsesh: Create and share climbs in Boardsesh. They don't go to MoonBoard's library.
publishing.official: Publish to the global problem library and appear in official rankings.

logging.boardsesh: Grade, stars and notes. Boardsesh never asks for height, weight or age.
logging.official: Reviews say it asks for height, weight and age before a send, and 'Not now' fails.

offline.boardsesh: Download the board, then search, climb and log offline; ticks sync later.
offline.official: Not documented. Reviews report 'Please Wait' screens that never finish loading.

logbook.boardsesh: Imports Moon's CSV; favourites live in your account and export as JSON.
logbook.official: Logbook and lists sync to Moon; favourites saved on the phone go on reinstall.

export.boardsesh: Export your logbook yourself, any time, as JSON
export.official: No in-app export; you email Moon for a CSV. Climbers report waiting weeks

crew.boardsesh: One queue of up to 500 climbs, shared from separate phones by invite link.
crew.official: Lists for warm-ups, projects and circuits. No shared queue documented.

training.boardsesh: 7 workout types, warm-up and cool-down stages, and a rest timer the crew shares.
training.official: Session tracking and lists; no workout builder or timer documented.

android.boardsesh: Any Android 7+ phone, no Google sign-in needed (email works).
android.official: Needs a Google-certified phone; one user's login failed with a 403 otherwise.

tablet.boardsesh: iPad sidebar, mini player and landscape player; Android tablets get a sidebar rail.
tablet.official: Has an iPad app; its iPad screenshots show the phone layout scaled up.

setup.title: Match your hold setup
setup.body: Pick the year on your holds, from 2010 to Mini 2025, then 25 or 40 degrees.

connect.title: Connect the LEDs
connect.body: Find your board in the picker, or open the browser app in Chrome or Edge and connect there.

warmup.title: Queue a warm-up
warmup.body: Add a few easy Benchmarks to the queue and let the rest timer pace you between climbs.

log.title: Log what you sent
log.body: Record each attempt and send with a grade and stars, and see the week's totals on your profile.

logbook.heading: Bring your MoonBoard logbook
logbook.lead: You ask Moon for a CSV by email, then import it. The import runs one way, into Boardsesh, and your Moon account stays as it is.

csv.title: Upload a MoonBoard CSV
csv.subtitle: Covers ticks logged at 25 and 40 degrees.

steps.s1: In Settings, then Connected apps, tap Request your data on the MoonBoard card.
steps.s2: Paste the copied request into an email to Moon, then import the CSV Moon sends.
steps.s3: Check the preview. Sends land in your logbook and unmatched problems are listed.

faq.heading: What MoonBoard climbers ask before switching

not-working.q: Why is the MoonBoard app not working or stuck on Please Wait?
not-working.a: Moon's help page says to swipe down on the problems list to refresh, or to log out and clear app data, since your logbook and lists stay on Moon's servers. If that fails, Moon says to reinstall and log in with the same details, and Boardsesh can light the board while you sort it out.

biometrics.q: Why does the MoonBoard app ask for my height and weight?
biometrics.a: Google Play reviews from July to October 2026 say it asks for height, weight and age before you can log a send. Boardsesh never asks for them.

android.q: Is there a MoonBoard app for Android?
android.a: Yes, Moon's own, but it needs a Google-certified phone. Boardsesh runs on Android 7 and up without that check.

leds.q: Will Boardsesh light my MoonBoard LEDs?
leds.a: Yes. It lights MoonBoard LEDs over Bluetooth from the app, or from Chrome or Edge on a laptop.

favourites.q: Do I lose my MoonBoard favourites if I reinstall the app?
favourites.a: Moon's July 2026 notice says favourites saved on the phone are not there after a reinstall, while the logbook and lists return from its servers. Boardsesh keeps favourites in your account.

csv.q: Can I import my MoonBoard logbook into Boardsesh?
csv.a: Yes. Ask Moon for your CSV (Boardsesh's MoonBoard card copies the request for you), then import it; it copies one way, for climbs logged at 25 and 40 degrees.

method.heading: How we compared
method.body: We read Moon's help pages, store listings and July 2026 notice, checked its reviews on 2026-11-24, and read the Android build's strings without running it. Controller support comes from a Boardsesh code audit dated 2026-11-20, not from a test on every box. Boardsesh has no tie to Moon Climbing.

cta.heading: Light your next MoonBoard problem with Boardsesh
cta.body: Free on iPhone, iPad, Android and in your browser, with no ads. Your MoonBoard CSV comes along.

meta.title: Woods Board App: Boardsesh vs the Official Woods App
meta.description: Boardsesh vs the official Woods Board app on 8x10 and 12x12 walls: matching and feet rules, a crew queue, setting climbs, and what stays in the Woods app.

hero.pill: Works with the Woods Board 8x10 and 12x12
hero.h1: Boardsesh vs the Woods Board app
hero.lead: Woods isn't an Aurora board: it has its own control box, its own Bluetooth format and its own app, and Boardsesh supports it on its own terms. Boardsesh lights both sizes, shows every climb's matching and feet rules, gives the crew one queue and logs Woods sends with seven other board brands and your spray wall. Your Woods account, the leaderboards and the official database stay in the Woods app.
hero.byline: A guide from Boardsesh. We make Boardsesh; board makers don't endorse it.

verdict.heading: Your Woods account, or one logbook for every board

pickIf.p1: You want matching and feet rules on every Woods climb before you pull on
pickIf.p2: You set problems on a phone and want only real holds offered
pickIf.p3: Your crew wants one queue on the 12x12, each adding from their own phone
pickIf.p4: You also log Kilter, Tension or MoonBoard and want one set of stats
pickIf.p5: You want the Woods catalogue on your phone for a garage with no signal

keepIf.k1: You climb for the weekly and all-time Woods leaderboards
keepIf.k2: You publish problems to the official Woods database
keepIf.k3: You want the full Woods catalogue behind your Woods account

verdict.bottomLine: The Woods app is where your account, the leaderboards and published climbs live. Boardsesh is a second way onto the same walls, built for crews and climbers with more than one board, with no Woods import and nothing written back.

only.heading: What Boardsesh adds to a Woods wall

rules.title: Matching and feet, shown separately
rules.body: Every Woods climb carries two rules: can you match, and can you use any feet. Boardsesh shows both on the climb and asks for both when you set one.

create.title: Set on the real hold map
create.body: Of the 12x12's 894 bolt slots, 725 carry a hold, and the editor offers only those 725. On the 8x10 it's 379 of 485.

crew.title: One queue at the Woods wall
crew.body: Friends add Woods problems from their own phones while one phone drives the control box, up to 500 climbs deep with undo.

faq.heading: What climbers ask about the Woods app

import.q: Can I import my Woods Board account into Boardsesh?
import.a: No. Boardsesh has no Woods import and doesn't write to the Woods app, so your logbook here starts fresh.

aurora.q: Is the Woods Board an Aurora board?
aurora.a: No. It uses its own control box, Bluetooth format and catalogue, and Boardsesh supports it separately from the six Aurora brands.

create.q: Can Boardsesh create climbs for the Woods Board?
create.a: Yes, on both sizes, with matching and feet rules. They're stored in Boardsesh, not published to the official Woods database.

flipped.q: Can I climb a Woods problem flipped in Boardsesh?
flipped.a: Yes. Mirror it on the wall and Boardsesh tracks your sends in each direction separately.

rating.q: How well rated is the Woods Board app?
rating.a: The US App Store shows 1.5 stars from 2 ratings, and Google Play shows none with 100+ installs. Two ratings say very little.

free.q: Is the Woods Board app free?
free.a: It's free to download, and the US App Store lists no purchases. Google Play lists in-app purchases of $14.99 to $35.99 without saying what they unlock.

meta.description: A free spray wall climbing app vs Stōkt (stokt), Crux and Retro Flash: hold detection, wall fees, offline use, one logbook with Kilter, and who wins where.

hero.pill: Works with any spray wall or home wall
hero.h1: Spray wall climbing apps: Boardsesh vs Stōkt, Crux and Retro Flash
hero.lead: Photograph your wall, fix the holds by hand, set problems and log sends, free. The same app also runs Kilter, Tension, MoonBoard, Woods and the other Aurora boards, so your spray wall and the gym boards share one logbook. Here is how Boardsesh compares with Stōkt, Crux and Retro Flash, including where they win.
hero.byline: A guide from Boardsesh. We make Boardsesh and compete with the apps compared here.

verdict.heading: Which spray wall app fits your wall

pickIf.p1: You own a home wall and don't want to pay per setup or per reset
pickIf.p2: You also climb a Kilter, Tension or MoonBoard and want one logbook
pickIf.p3: You climb in a garage or basement with no signal
pickIf.p4: Your crew wants one queue on the wall, from phones, an iPad or a laptop
pickIf.p5: You want LEDs on your wall on a budget, with a WLED controller

keepIf.k1: You want to climb in Stōkt's network of more than 2,000 walls
keepIf.k2: You will pay for a ready-made LED kit, sold by Stōkt in the EU and UK
keepIf.k3: You need mirrored climbs on a symmetric wall, as Stōkt and Retro Flash offer

verdict.bottomLine: For a wall of your own, Boardsesh costs nothing, works offline and puts your spray wall in the same logbook as every gym board you climb. Crux is also free for home walls and scans fast; Stōkt has the most walls and will map every hold for you, for a fee.

one-logbook.title: Your spray wall and the gym boards, one logbook

offline.title: Climb with no signal
offline.body: Your walls, their climbs and your logbook are kept on the phone, and sends sync when you're back online. Adding a new wall needs signal.

free.title: No wall fee, no yearly pass
free.body: Adding a wall, setting problems and resetting it cost nothing, with no ads and no paid tier. Each account can keep up to 10 live walls.

comparison.heading: Boardsesh, Stōkt, Crux and Retro Flash side by side

faq.heading: What climbers ask about spray wall apps

best.q: What is the best spray wall app?
best.a: It depends on your wall. For a free home wall with offline use and one logbook shared with your gym boards, pick Boardsesh; for the biggest network of public walls, Stōkt, and Crux is a strong free option too.

stokt-alt.q: Is there a free alternative to Stōkt (stokt)?
stokt-alt.a: Boardsesh and Crux are both free for home walls. Stōkt's FAQ lists a fee per wall setup and per reset with 12 months of access, while its app has said since August 2026 that self-scanned walls start free.

one-app.q: Can one app run my spray wall and my Kilter board?
one-app.a: Boardsesh can: it runs Kilter, Tension, MoonBoard, Woods and the other Aurora boards next to your spray wall, with one logbook. Stōkt, Crux and Retro Flash don't document board support.

retro.q: Does Retro Flash cost money now?
retro.a: Retro Flash is a free download, but home walls and gyms have needed a yearly pass since version 2.1.7 in July 2026. The US App Store lists the Home Wall Year Pass at $4.99.

leds.q: Can I light my spray wall with LEDs?
leds.a: Yes, through WLED, a low-cost open-source LED controller you wire yourself and connect over Wi-Fi. Stōkt sells its own LED kit in the EU and UK.

offline.q: Does a spray wall app work without signal?
offline.a: Boardsesh keeps your walls, climbs and logbook on the phone and syncs sends when you're back online. Stōkt, Crux and Retro Flash don't document offline use.
